rationale: The retry-cycle successor executed in a clean copy (87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4, completed, exit 0) and all eleven comparisons are complete and evaluated as holds: three consecutive invocations on the re-added voter never completed while the cluster kept committing proposals from the never-removed member in the same intervals. This update attributes that retained interpretation to the retry experiment, replaces the previous 'single invocation' basis with the repeated-nonprogress basis, records the observation as durable knowledge with receipt indices, and withdraws the limitation that only a single invocation was observed.

knowledge.statement: In the retained three-node scenario, invocations on the re-added voter never completed and never delivered while other members' proposals were committed in the same intervals: invocation 1 (2500 ms context) had not returned after 1200 ms and released only with 'context deadline exceeded' at 2501 ms with no node holding its payload; retries 2 and 3 (900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) also had not returned and their payloads were absent, and in each retry interval a proposal by never-removed node 2 returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes. After the leader changed from 1 to 2 at term 2, the same invocation on the re-added voter returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks delivered; node 3 removed and re-added by committed conf changes with leader 1 unchanged throughout the non-completing invocations; each retry uses an independent context and operation id.

interpretations.joint_history: All three receipts run the same fixed scenario lineage: 3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-experiment (executed as 43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad) and its successors 48ce57b251a644edaaf9d17731df0b25-experiment (a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f) and baee4030bf1e4f229c46ece8d0ddc365-experiment (87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4), each registered with previous_id and a revision_reason. All three build the same configuration {1,2,3} from the same storage ConfState, elect leader 1 at term 1, apply the same committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes on node 3, use the same witness/control/repair operation ids, payloads, phases, deadlines and windows, and force the same campaign of node 2 into term 2; the successors add event naming and then the retry/progress cases without changing the earlier ones. The witnesses agree field for field at the corresponding indices (witness 7/8/9 in all three; control 11/12; repair 15/16 or 25/26), so the difference is a property of the fixed scenario rather than of one run.
interpretations.rationale: Three retained executions agree and the successor adds the missing bounded-progress element. In 87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4: node 3 applied its own re-admission (index 4: change add, ok true, voter true, leader 1, term 1) and its configuration listed it as a voter with leader 1 (index 5); the admitted invocation (index 6) had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7: returned false, err empty, voter true, leader 1), released only when the caller's deadline expired (index 8: 'context deadline exceeded', 2501 ms), and left its payload absent from every node's committed entries (index 9: present false, observed_nodes null). During the same stable-leader period the never-removed member's invocation returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 11, 12). Two independent retry attempts on node 3 (distinct operation ids, 900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) also never completed (indices 14 and 19: returned false at 800 ms and 801 ms, voter true, leader 1) and were not committed, while in each of those intervals a fresh proposal by node 2 returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes (indices 17 and 22: present true, observed_nodes [1,2,3] and [3,1,2]). After node 3 observed the leader change 1->2 at term 2 (index 23) the same invocation returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 25, 26). The source account matches: the run loop's proposal gate is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), node.go:377 (no leader) and node.go:426 (local member removed) and read for proposals at node.go:525, and a re-admission cannot match the removal guard because the local Progress entry is already gone (node.go:401-412), so MsgProp is offered to a nil channel and can end only via the caller's context or node stop. The snapshot's own expectation (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader and expects acceptance once a leader is known, which is the condition node 3 satisfies while blocked; the control and the two interval controls exclude cluster-wide stalls, and the post-leader-change case excludes a defect in node 3's own state machine. The result is a repeated, signalled-free non-completion of a member's proposal duty under a stable leader, with no source-enabled repair other than an unrelated leader change.
counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised ('propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs'); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.

Each witnessed invocation ends when the caller's own context expires, so the non-completion is measured against caller-supplied intervals rather than an unbounded wait; the payload is never delivered or rejected inside those intervals.
The snapshots include a successful path in the same run (indices 12, 17, 22, 26), showing proposals are neither generally dropped nor generally blocked.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were 'unknown' because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose has no such gate. No ticks were delivered and delivery was reliable, so no timing or network-fault characterization is claimed.

Only the voter-removal form was executed; other transitions that delete the local Progress entry are variants of the same cause and were not executed separately. The same gate also covers Node.ProposeConfChange (node.go:496-502 via stepWithWaitOption), which was not executed.

The harness stops the node at test end, so the release of an invocation issued with an unbounded context while the node keeps running was not observed; the measured intervals are the caller-supplied deadlines.
